masking.py:113-126 splits at every non-isalnum char. _split_chunk (85-110) groups runs by class U/L/D, so lower-to-upper and letter/digit boundaries split. An upper run followed by a lower run splits before the last capital (103-105), so APIKey gives api, key. The plural exception (100-101) applies only when the lower run is exactly 's' and is followed by a digit run or the end of the chunk, so PINs gives pins. PINsKey does not trigger it, which matches 'non-letter or end'. Entries use the same splitter (129-134). _word_matches (148-149) accepts the word, word+s or word+es. _label_matches (152-157) requires consecutive in-order windows. Traced inputs: PINS gives the single word pins and matches pin+s; APIKeys gives api, keys and matches key; OTPSecret gives otp, secret; zip_code and COLUMN_KEY split on the underscore. All agree with the doc text.
